contentBlocks.body:
**Objective.** Review a change as someone who has not seen the author's working session.

This is a real project lab in projects/inventory-desk, also available from the Projects page as a source download. Work in an isolated copy of the reference project so you can compare your change with a known baseline. Read A focused product or test diff before editing. Trace one request from the UI or test through the boundary that owns the behavior.

contentBlocks.code:
git diff --stat
git diff --check
dotnet test InventoryDesk.Tests

contentBlocks.body:
**Acceptance criteria.** The review explains the trigger, expected before/after behavior, test evidence and any limitation without relying on conversational history.

**Make a meaningful variation.** Review a price-validation change and identify the missing zero-price or maximum-value boundary. Write the observable expectation before editing the implementation. If the variation exposes a defect, keep the smallest failing fixture as a regression test.
Review rubric: Comments point to concrete cases and distinguish a correctness problem from a preference.

**Explain the boundary.** Which review comment is most actionable? Describe both a successful case and a rejected or missing-data case. Compare actual output with the acceptance criteria, including status codes, persisted values, and user-visible feedback where relevant.

**Evidence to keep.** Save the focused test result, a short before/after diff, and a note explaining one tradeoff. Completing the quiz records this lesson's concepts; it does not run the companion checks or certify that the project milestone is finished.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which review comment is most actionable?

choices: A vague request to improve quality
A demand to rewrite unrelated code
A specific input that causes incorrect behavior and an expected result
payload.answer: A specific input that causes incorrect behavior and an expected result
